buff.audience.how.0: A player can take each buff once per game, no more than one per question and only before answering.
buff.audience.how.1: The player takes the buff, and the other players get “… asks the room: what do you think?” with their name.
buff.audience.how.2: In classic rounds those who have already answered vote; on the board — everyone except whoever picked the cell.
buff.audience.how.3: The player sees percentages for the options, and for text, number and slider — the room's guesses.
buff.audience.how.4: If the question has a timer, the player gets +15 seconds while the room votes.
buff.audience.limits.0: Only simple types: options, several correct, yes/no, text, number, slider.
buff.audience.limits.1: At least one player who can vote is needed.
buff.audience.limits.2: Doesn't work on “Who am I?” or pin on the map.
buff.audience.limits.3: Doesn't work on “100 to 1”: the room's votes would give away the board.
buff.audience.limits.5: In “Millionaire” it's a separate ladder lifeline: it's turned on in the round, works once per ladder and doesn't use up the buff.
buff.audience.limits.6: In a team game members of the other teams vote: in classic rounds — of the teams that have already answered, on the board — everyone except the team that picked the cell.
buff.audience.limits.7: Buffs don't work in a blitz, on blitz cells, in the final, in “All in”, “Knockout” and “Millionaire”, on “chain” and “sorting” questions, on connection walls, polls and word clouds, or in duels.
buff.audience.points.0: Points as usual. The room's votes neither give nor take points.
buff.audience.tip.0: In classic rounds the buff is more useful near the end of the timer, when most have already answered.
buff.audience.title: Ask the room
buff.audience.what: The other players vote for 15 seconds on what answer they would give.
buff.double.how.0: A player can take each buff once per game, no more than one per question and only before answering.
buff.double.how.1: The player takes the buff before answering. The stage and the console show who took the buff.
buff.double.limits.0: Only classic rounds and the board on your turn, including out-loud cells.
buff.double.limits.1: Buffs don't work in a blitz, on blitz cells, in the final, in “All in”, “Knockout” and “Millionaire”, on “chain” and “sorting” questions, on connection walls, polls and word clouds, or in duels.
buff.double.points.0: Only positive points are doubled, together with the streak bonus. The minus for a mistake isn't doubled.
buff.double.points.1: The cell's mark and the round multiplier multiply on top.
buff.double.points.2: On “100 to 1” the board points are doubled.
buff.double.points.3: On a bluff it doubles both the truth and the points for those fooled.
buff.double.tip.0: Best value on an expensive ×2 or ×3 cell.
buff.double.title: Double points
buff.double.what: Doubles the player's points for this question.
buff.fifty.how.0: A player can take each buff once per game, no more than one per question and only before answering.
buff.fifty.how.1: The player taps the buff button under the question twice — the wrong options are crossed out on their phone, and on a board cell on the stage too.
buff.fifty.how.2: How many are removed: of 3 options — 1, of 4 — 2, of 6 — 3. In “several correct” — half the wrong ones, but one wrong option always stays; if there are fewer than two wrong ones, the buff doesn't work.
buff.fifty.limits.0: Only questions with options (at least 3 options) in classic rounds and on the board on your turn.
buff.fifty.limits.1: Doesn't work on “Who am I?” or pin on the map.
buff.fifty.limits.2: Doesn't work on “100 to 1”: there are no options.
buff.fifty.limits.4: In “Millionaire” it's a separate ladder lifeline: it's turned on in the round, works once per ladder and doesn't use up the buff.
buff.fifty.limits.5: Buffs don't work in a blitz, on blitz cells, in the final, in “All in”, “Knockout” and “Millionaire”, on “chain” and “sorting” questions, on connection walls, polls and word clouds, or in duels.
buff.fifty.what: Removes some of the wrong options for the player who took the buff.
buff.guard.how.0: A player can take each buff once per game, no more than one per question and only before answering.
buff.guard.how.1: The player takes the buff before answering. If the answer is wrong, partial or missing, the streak doesn't break, it just doesn't grow.
buff.guard.how.2: The next correct answer continues the streak and gives the bonus if the streak is already long enough.
buff.guard.limits.0: Only rounds with a streak bonus (the “Streaks” setting).
buff.guard.limits.2: In a team game the streak belongs to the team: whoever answers takes the buff.
buff.guard.limits.3: Buffs don't work in a blitz, on blitz cells, in the final, in “All in”, “Knockout” and “Millionaire”, on “chain” and “sorting” questions, on connection walls, polls and word clouds, or in duels.
buff.guard.points.0: Points for the question itself are as usual, including the minus for a mistake.
buff.guard.points.1: The streak bonus is only awarded for a correct answer.
buff.guard.tip.0: Take it when the streak is already long and the question is hard.
buff.guard.title: Safety net
buff.guard.what: A mistake doesn't break the streak of correct answers.
buff.hint.how.0: A player can take each buff once per game, no more than one per question and only before answering.
buff.hint.how.1: If the “Hint” field is filled in the editor, the player sees it straight away.
buff.hint.how.2: If not, the console shows “… asks for a hint” with the player's name. Write a hint and press “Send”, or give a hint out loud and press “Gave a hint out loud”.
buff.hint.limits.0: Only classic rounds and the board on your turn, including out-loud cells.
buff.hint.limits.1: Doesn't work on a bluff: a hint would give away the truth.
buff.hint.limits.2: In “Millionaire” it's a separate ladder lifeline: it's turned on in the round, works once per ladder and doesn't use up the buff.
buff.hint.limits.3: In a team game the whole team sees the hint text.
buff.hint.limits.4: Buffs don't work in a blitz, on blitz cells, in the final, in “All in”, “Knockout” and “Millionaire”, on “chain” and “sorting” questions, on connection walls, polls and word clouds, or in duels.
buff.hint.tip.0: Fill in hints in the editor for hard questions — you won't have to make them up on the spot.
buff.hint.title: Host's hint
buff.hint.what: The player gets a hint for this question.
buff.letter.how.0: A player can take each buff once per game, no more than one per question and only before answering.
buff.letter.how.1: The player takes the buff, and above the answer field appears, for example, “L _ _ _ · _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ (12)”: a dot is a space, hyphens and apostrophes stay in place.
buff.letter.how.2: The first spelling from the editor is used, so put the main one first.
buff.letter.limits.2: Can't be taken after “Swap question”: one buff per question.
buff.letter.limits.3: In a team game the whole team sees the letter.
buff.letter.limits.4: Buffs don't work in a blitz, on blitz cells, in the final, in “All in”, “Knockout” and “Millionaire”, on “chain” and “sorting” questions, on connection walls, polls and word clouds, or in duels.
buff.letter.points.0: A correct or partial answer earns 75% of the normal points. The minus for a mistake doesn't change.
buff.letter.tip.0: A lifesaver when the answer is on the tip of your tongue.
buff.letter.title: First letter
buff.letter.what: The player's phone shows the first letter of the answer and the number of letters.
buff.peek.how.0: A player can take each buff once per game, no more than one per question and only before answering.
buff.peek.how.1: The player taps the buff twice — a list opens of those whose answer has already been sent. The player picks one.
buff.peek.how.2: The phone shows the chosen answer — without a mark of whether it's right or wrong.
buff.peek.how.3: The player who was peeked at sees “👀 Someone peeked at your answer: Olya”, and the stage shows “👀 Peek: Olya → Petro”.
buff.peek.limits.0: Only classic rounds and simple types: options, several correct, yes/no, text, number, slider.
buff.peek.limits.1: At least one already submitted answer to the main question (not a spare) is needed.
buff.peek.limits.2: Only a submitted answer is visible, not a draft.
buff.peek.limits.4: In a team game you see another team's answer; whoever answers takes it.
buff.peek.limits.5: Buffs don't work in a blitz, on blitz cells, in the final, in “All in”, “Knockout” and “Millionaire”, on “chain” and “sorting” questions, on connection walls, polls and word clouds, or in duels.
buff.peek.points.0: Points as usual: the player still answers themselves.
buff.peek.tip.0: More useful near the end of the timer, when many have answered.
buff.peek.title: Peek
buff.peek.what: The player sees another player's already submitted answer to this question.
buff.retry.how.0: A player can take each buff once per game, no more than one per question and only before answering.
buff.retry.how.1: The first answer is wrong — the phone says “Wrong, one more try”.
buff.retry.how.2: The first answer is partial — the player chooses: “Keep” the points or “Try again”.
buff.retry.how.3: If time runs out before the second answer, the first one counts.
buff.retry.limits.0: Only simple types: options, several correct, yes/no, text, number, slider.
buff.retry.limits.1: Doesn't work out loud or on the board with manual checking.
buff.retry.limits.2: Doesn't work on an emerging picture.
buff.retry.limits.3: Doesn't work on “Who am I?” (one answer only) or pin on the map.
buff.retry.limits.4: Doesn't work on “100 to 1”: the player already writes several answers.
buff.retry.limits.6: In a team game it's the team's second try: the captain takes it, and “already used” applies to the team.
buff.retry.limits.7: Buffs don't work in a blitz, on blitz cells, in the final, in “All in”, “Knockout” and “Millionaire”, on “chain” and “sorting” questions, on connection walls, polls and word clouds, or in duels.
buff.retry.points.0: The second answer counts (or the first one if kept).
buff.retry.tip.0: Most useful on text answers and numbers.
buff.retry.title: Second try
buff.retry.what: After a wrong answer the player answers again.
buff.risk.how.0: A player can take each buff once per game, no more than one per question and only before answering.
buff.risk.how.1: The player takes the buff before answering. The stage and the console show who's taking the risk.
buff.risk.how.2: If there's still no answer when time runs out, the minus is applied when the question closes.
buff.risk.limits.0: Only classic rounds and the board on your turn, including out-loud cells.
buff.risk.limits.1: Only questions with a clear-cut answer: options, several correct, yes/no, text, number, slider, “Who am I?” and pin on the map.
buff.risk.limits.2: Doesn't stack with “Double points”: one buff per question.
buff.risk.limits.4: In a team game the whole team takes the risk: whoever answers takes the buff.
buff.risk.limits.5: Buffs don't work in a blitz, on blitz cells, in the final, in “All in”, “Knockout” and “Millionaire”, on “chain” and “sorting” questions, on connection walls, polls and word clouds, or in duels.

buff.risk.points.1: Wrong or no answer — minus the question's full value with the round multiplier (on the board — the cell's value with its mark), even in a round with no penalty.
buff.risk.points.3: Your judgement and appeals follow the same rules: “Correct” gives ×3.
buff.risk.tip.0: For the confident: on an expensive cell, risk is either a leap ahead or a pit.
buff.risk.title: Risk
buff.risk.what: A correct answer earns three times the points, but a mistake or silence costs the question's full value.
buff.scope.how.0: A player can take each buff once per game, no more than one per question and only before answering.
buff.scope.how.1: Slider: “The answer is between 1590 and 1650” — a range of 20% of the scale; the correct answer is at a random place within it.
buff.scope.how.2: Number: a range of ±10% of the correct answer (at least ±2), also shifted at random.
buff.scope.how.3: Pin on the map: the map zooms into the quarter of the base with the target; the frame stays visible even after zooming out.
buff.scope.limits.0: Only number, slider and pin on the map.
buff.scope.limits.2: Can't be taken after “Swap question”: one buff per question.
buff.scope.limits.3: In a team game the whole team sees the range.
buff.scope.limits.4: Buffs don't work in a blitz, on blitz cells, in the final, in “All in”, “Knockout” and “Millionaire”, on “chain” and “sorting” questions, on connection walls, polls and word clouds, or in duels.
buff.scope.tip.0: Strongest on a slider with a wide scale: years, kilometres, percentages.
buff.scope.title: Binoculars
buff.scope.what: Narrows the search: shows a range where the answer lies, or zooms into the part of the map with the target.
buff.shield.how.0: A player can take each buff once per game, no more than one per question and only before answering.
buff.shield.how.1: The player takes the shield before answering. If the answer would have cost a minus, the player gets 0.
buff.shield.limits.0: Only where a mistake costs points (the “minus” rule).
buff.shield.limits.1: Buffs don't work in a blitz, on blitz cells, in the final, in “All in”, “Knockout” and “Millionaire”, on “chain” and “sorting” questions, on connection walls, polls and word clouds, or in duels.
buff.shield.points.0: A minus becomes 0. A correct answer counts as usual.
buff.shield.points.1: On a bluff it saves you from the minus for a picked fib.
buff.shield.tip.0: Only makes sense in rounds with the “minus” penalty — in others the buff can't be taken.
buff.shield.title: Shield
buff.swap.how.0: A player can take each buff once per game, no more than one per question and only before answering.
buff.swap.how.1: The player takes the buff, and the next unused spare appears on their phone; the others answer the main one.
buff.swap.how.2: On the board everyone sees the spare, since only whoever picked the cell answers. It comes from the same category if the categories have their own spares.
buff.swap.how.3: Each spare is given out only once per game.
buff.swap.limits.0: The “Swap” buff can only be allowed if there are spare questions.
buff.swap.limits.1: Spares are simple types only (options, several correct, yes/no, text, number, slider) with no video, audio or emerging picture.
buff.swap.limits.2: Doesn't work on a bluff: the others' choice depends on that same question.
buff.swap.limits.3: Buffs don't work in a blitz, on blitz cells, in the final, in “All in”, “Knockout” and “Millionaire”, on “chain” and “sorting” questions, on connection walls, polls and word clouds, or in duels.
buff.swap.points.0: The value, multipliers and penalty come from the current question.
buff.swap.points.1: On a question with a timer the player has at least 20 seconds after the swap; the speed bonus is counted from the moment of the swap.
buff.swap.tip.0: Fill in general spares for classic rounds and 1–2 spares in each board category.
buff.swap.title: Swap question
buff.swap.what: The player gets another question from the spares instead of the current one.
buff.time.how.0: A player can take each buff once per game, no more than one per question and only before answering.
buff.time.how.1: The player's timer is extended, the others answer in the normal time.
buff.time.how.2: When everyone else has answered, the console shows “Waiting: …” with the player's time — you can press “Don't wait” and close the question.
buff.time.limits.0: Only questions with a timer (not with video) in classic rounds and on the board.
buff.time.limits.1: Doesn't work on a bluff: both timers are shared.
buff.time.limits.2: Buffs don't work in a blitz, on blitz cells, in the final, in “All in”, “Knockout” and “Millionaire”, on “chain” and “sorting” questions, on connection walls, polls and word clouds, or in duels.
buff.time.points.0: Points as usual. The speed bonus is counted from the normal time: an answer in the extra seconds counts as an answer in the last second.
buff.time.points.1: On “Who am I?” extra time doesn't reveal new clues — they're all open already.
buff.time.tip.0: A lifesaver on long questions — ordering and pairs.
buff.time.title: Extra time
cell.blitz.how.0: By phone with automatic checking it's instant: everyone answers once, and you press “Accept answer” in turn.
cell.blitz.how.1: By phone with manual checking, players press “Answer”: each has {defaultAnswerWindow} seconds to answer, as many tries as they like, and you judge.
cell.blitz.how.2: Out loud: players press “Answer” and answer out loud in turn, and you judge.
cell.blitz.limits.0: No buffs on a blitz cell.
cell.blitz.limits.1: Sorting can't be on a blitz cell.
cell.blitz.limits.2: Not for “Who am I?” or pin on the map.
cell.blitz.points.0: The first correct player gets value × mark × the round multiplier, and if it's whoever picked the cell — twice as much.
cell.blitz.points.1: A wrong try costs 0: the round penalty doesn't apply here.
cell.blitz.points.2: The “Minus for all” penalty: everyone except whoever got it right loses the cell's value (× mark × multiplier), including those who stayed silent.
cell.blitz.tip.0: A blitz on an expensive question wakes up those waiting for their turn.
cell.blitz.title: Blitz cell
cell.blitz.what: A cell everyone answers: the first to answer correctly gets the points.
cell.marks.how.0: Players and the stage don't see the marks on the board — it's a surprise: after the cell flips, everyone sees “×2!” or “×3!”.
cell.marks.how.1: On the console the marks are always visible.
cell.marks.points.0: Everything is multiplied: points for a correct answer, the “minus” penalty and “Minus for all”.
cell.marks.points.1: The round multiplier applies on top: ×2 in a round with a ×3 multiplier gives ×6.
cell.marks.tip.0: One or two marks are enough for a board; put them on hard questions.
cell.marks.title: ×2 and ×3
cell.marks.what: A mark doubles or triples the cell's value.
cell.normal.how.0: Only the player whose turn it is answers — by phone or out loud, as set for the cell. The others see the question on the stage.
cell.normal.how.1: On a normal cell only they can take buffs, too.
cell.normal.limits.0: A connection wall — by phone only.
cell.normal.points.0: Value × mark × the round multiplier. With the “minus” penalty, a mistake or silence takes away the same amount.
cell.normal.tip.0: Most board cells are normal; place the special ones sparingly.
cell.normal.title: Normal cell
cell.normal.what: A question for whoever picked the cell.
cell.voice.how.0: The player's phone says “Answer out loud”, the question is on the stage.
cell.voice.how.1: In a question with options or yes/no, tap the option the player said on the console — the stage will highlight it.
cell.voice.how.2: Judge it: “Accept”, “Partly” (with the “partly” rule) or “Don't count”.
cell.voice.how.3: “Who am I?” on an out-loud cell: you reveal the next clue with the “Reveal clue” button; the points follow the clue on which the answer was given.
cell.voice.limits.1: Pin on the map — only a normal cell answered by phone.
cell.voice.limits.4: A debuff doesn't fire on an out-loud cell: it waits for a question where the player answers by phone.
cell.voice.points.0: As on a normal cell: value × mark × the round multiplier, the “minus” penalty applies.
cell.voice.tip.0: Good for questions where the explanation matters, and for players without a phone to hand.
cell.voice.tip.1: Players take buffs from their phone on an out-loud cell too, except “Second try”.
cell.voice.title: Answer out loud
cell.voice.what: The player answers out loud, and you judge.
debuff.bubbles.how.0: You cast the debuff for free from the player's row on the console (“Debuff”), and players buy it for rivals with points. It kicks in on the next question where the target answers by phone and is connected to the game. Freeze lasts a few seconds, the other debuffs last until the end of the question.
debuff.bubbles.how.1: A bubble catches the tap: the option under it can't be pressed until the bubble is popped.
debuff.bubbles.limits.0: On polls and word clouds the debuff doesn't fire — it waits for the next question with points. There are no debuffs in “All in”: a waiting debuff kicks in in the next round. In “Knockout” a debuff only works on the living and doesn't fire during a trial: it can't be cast on a ghost, and one that was waiting for them kicks in in the next round. There are no debuffs in “Millionaire”: a waiting debuff kicks in in the next round.
debuff.bubbles.limits.1: In a team game the debuff is cast on the team and only works on the phone of whoever answers (without a choice — the captain's); the rest of the team sees a mark. The captain buys debuffs with team points.
debuff.bubbles.limits.2: If “Reduce Motion” is on in the phone, the torch and bubbles have no animation, and the flip is instant.
debuff.bubbles.points.0: The debuff doesn't change points — it only gets in the way; the buyer pays its price.
debuff.bubbles.tip.0: Like fog, it makes the target spend a few seconds — but it's more fun.
debuff.bubbles.title: Bubbles
debuff.bubbles.what: 12 bubbles cover the answers; each one pops with a tap.

question.bluff.how.0: You write a fact with a gap (“…”), the truth (with other spellings) and 2–3 spare fibs.
question.bluff.how.1: The “fib phase” has its own timer: everyone writes a fake answer. The phone won't accept the truth (in any spelling): “That's the truth! Make up something else”. Identical fibs are merged into one.
question.bluff.how.2: The phase ends when everyone has written, time runs out or you press “To voting”.
question.bluff.how.3: The “voting phase” has its own timer too: everyone sees the fibs, the truth and, if there are fewer than {bluffOptions} options, your spare fibs — shuffled, without authors. You can't pick your own fib; those who didn't write can still pick. You can close voting early with the “Close voting” button.
question.bluff.how.4: Remove an offensive fib with the “Remove” button (only during voting): it disappears, and its authors get nothing for it. Whoever picked it picks again.
question.bluff.how.5: At the reveal you open the options one by one (“Reveal option k of n”) or all together (“Reveal all”): least picked first, who was fooled and whose fib it is; the truth comes last. The phone shows the result when the truth is revealed.
question.bluff.limits.0: A fib and the truth — up to {bluffLie} characters; {minBluffSpares}–{maxBluffSpares} spare fibs.
question.bluff.limits.1: Classic rounds only: all players are needed at the same time.
question.bluff.limits.2: Only “Double points” and “Shield” work (the shield — with the “minus” penalty). The other buffs: the time is shared, a hint would give away the truth, a swap would break everyone else's choice.
question.bluff.limits.3: No video: the fib phase must have a timer.
question.bluff.limits.4: In a team game there's one fib and one pick per team (the captain submits); a team can't pick its own fib.
question.bluff.points.0: Picked the truth — the question's value. Picking the truth is a correct answer: streak, accuracy, achievements.
question.bluff.points.1: For every player fooled by your fib — half the value. Co-authors of an identical fib each get it.
question.bluff.points.2: The round multiplier applies to everything. There's no speed bonus.
question.bluff.points.3: The “minus” penalty only hits those who picked a fib and earned nothing.
question.bluff.tip.0: The fact should be strange but true — then the fibs sound just as convincing.
question.bluff.tip.1: Add spellings of the truth: “Barca” alongside “Barcelona” — then it can't be submitted as a fib.
question.bluff.tip.2: Spare fibs save a game of three: there'll be up to five options.
question.bluff.title: Bluff
question.bluff.what: Players make up fake answers and then look for the truth among each other's fibs.
question.boolean.tip.0: You can guess with a 50% chance, so set a lower value or turn on the “minus” penalty.
question.boolean.title: Yes or no
question.boolean.what: A statement to agree or disagree with.
question.chain.how.0: Players see the first word, and the next one only as its first letter and the number of letters.
question.chain.how.1: Everyone guesses at their own pace. “Hint” reveals one more letter but adds seconds to the player's time.
question.chain.how.2: The stage shows players' progress without the words themselves.
question.chain.limits.1: Only in a classic round and in the final.
question.chain.points.0: Whoever completes the whole chain gets points: the fastest — the full value, the rest — less, down to half the value for whoever finished right on time.
question.chain.points.2: In the final a completed chain gives plus the stake, and an unfinished one costs minus the stake.
question.chain.tip.0: Check the chain out loud: each word should follow naturally from the previous one.
question.chain.title: Word chain
question.chain.what: A chain of linked words: everyone sees the first one, the rest have to be guessed in turn.
question.clues.how.0: You set {minClues}–{maxClues} clues, the answer's spellings and the interval between clues.
question.clues.how.1: The first clue is visible straight away, the next ones every N seconds (large on the stage, on the phones as a list with a countdown to the next). The player can write the answer at any time, but only once.
question.clues.how.2: Pausing and holding stop the countdown: the next clue opens after the rest of the interval.
question.clues.how.3: The switch “Clues are revealed: by the timer / each at own pace”. “Each at own pace”: every player first sees the first clue and presses “Another clue” on their phone themselves; a clue can't be closed. The timer is shared.
question.clues.how.4: In “each at own pace” mode the stage only shows the first clue and a line with how many each has revealed (“Olya 1 · Petro 3”), and at the reveal — all the clues and the clue each answered on. On the console, in “Live answers”, next to each player there's “clue 3/5”, and after the answer — “on clue 3”.
question.clues.how.5: In a team game clues are revealed by whoever answers for the team; teammates see the same ones.
question.clues.how.6: On an out-loud board cell clues don't open by time: you reveal the next one with the “Reveal clue” button on the console. The console shows all clues marked “revealed” and the clue each player answered on.
question.clues.limits.0: Only classic rounds and a normal board cell (by phone or out loud).
question.clues.limits.1: 50/50, “Second try” and “Ask the room” don't work.
question.clues.limits.2: A clue is up to {clueText} characters; interval {minClueSeconds}–{maxClueSeconds} s. On an out-loud cell no interval is needed, but with a timer the time must still be at least (n − 1) × {minClueSeconds} + {clueTailSeconds} s, where n is the number of clues.
question.clues.limits.3: The last clue must open at least {clueTailSeconds} s before the time is up: (number of clues − 1) × interval + {clueTailSeconds} s no more than the question's time.
question.clues.limits.4: “Each at own pace”: there's no interval, the last-clue rule doesn't apply, but the question's time is at least {selfCluesMinTime} s.
question.clues.limits.5: On an out-loud cell “each at own pace” doesn't work: you reveal the clues with a button on the console.
question.clues.limits.6: The “Another clue” button won't reveal a clue after answering, during a pause, on the intro or after time is up. Extra time doesn't reveal new clues — the player reveals them.
question.clues.points.0: An answer after clue k of n — value × (n − k + 1) / n: with 5 clues that's 100, 80, 60, 40 and 20% of the value.
question.clues.points.1: A wrong answer — 0 (with the “minus” penalty — minus the value).
question.clues.points.2: A correct answer counts as correct on any clue: it goes into the streak, accuracy and achievements.
question.clues.points.3: There's no speed bonus — the decline is already built in.
question.clues.points.4: On an out-loud cell the points follow the clue that was open at the moment you judged.
question.clues.points.5: In “each at own pace” mode the value depends on how many clues this player had revealed when answering: with 5 clues, one — 100%, three — 60%. Whoever doesn't answer gets 0.
question.clues.tip.0: The first clue should be really hard, the last one almost the answer.
question.clues.tip.1: An interval of 6–10 seconds gives time to read the clue out loud.
question.clues.tip.2: In “each at own pace” mode give 40–60 s: players need time to decide whether to take the risk.
question.clues.title: Who am I?
question.clues.what: Clues are revealed one at a time, from hardest to easiest; whoever recognises the answer sooner gets more. Or each player reveals clues themselves — then the fewer they reveal, the more they get.
question.match.how.0: The player taps an item on the left, then on the right, and presses “Answer”.
question.match.how.1: Players see the right column shuffled.
question.match.points.0: The value only when all pairs are correct; otherwise 0.
question.match.tip.0: Items on the right of the same length and look stop players guessing a pair by its shape.
question.match.title: Pairs
question.match.what: Each item on the left has to be matched with its pair on the right.
question.multi.how.0: The player marks the options and presses “Answer”.
question.multi.points.0: The value only when all the correct ones are marked and no extra ones; otherwise 0.
question.multi.tip.0: If you don't want players to guess, say in the text how many are correct.
question.multi.title: Several correct options
question.multi.what: You have to mark all the correct options.
question.numeric.how.0: The player types a number and presses “Answer”.
question.numeric.points.0: Deviation 0: only the exact number gets the value.
question.numeric.points.1: With a deviation: the exact number — the full value, at the edge of the deviation — half, in between — proportionally; beyond it — 0.
question.numeric.points.2: On the board an inexact number within the deviation only gives points with the “partly” rule.
question.numeric.points.3: In a blitz, on a blitz cell and in the final, only the exact number counts.
question.numeric.tip.0: For dates and big numbers, set a deviation, for example year ± 5.
question.numeric.tip.1: Want players to drag rather than type? Use “Slider”.
question.numeric.title: Number
question.order.how.0: The player moves the rows with the ↑ ↓ arrows and presses “Answer”.
question.order.how.1: The “What's at the top” and “What's at the bottom” labels (for example, “Largest”) hint at the direction.
question.order.points.0: Everything in place — the question's value. Otherwise — a share for each item in its place (3 of 5 — 60%).
question.order.points.1: On the board only the “partly” rule gives the share.
question.order.points.2: In a blitz and the final — only a fully correct order.
question.order.tip.0: Write the items in the correct order: players will see them shuffled.
question.order.title: Ordering
question.order.what: The items have to be put in the right order.
question.pin.how.0: The base is a built-in “World”, “Europe” or “Ukraine” map or your own picture. You place the correct pin and set two circles: the full-points radius and the zero radius (3 and 15 by default).
question.pin.how.1: The player taps the map (the pin can be moved until “Answer”) and zooms with two fingers or the buttons.
question.pin.how.2: At the reveal the stage shows all pins with nicknames, the correct pin and the circles; the closest player is highlighted. You see the live pins and the correct pin already during the question.
question.pin.limits.0: Only classic rounds and a normal board cell answered by phone.
question.pin.limits.1: Full points — up to {pinMaxFullRadius}%, zero — up to {pinMaxZeroRadius}%; the second radius is bigger than the first.
question.pin.limits.2: 50/50 doesn't work here: there are no options. “Second try” and “Ask the room” don't work either.
question.pin.limits.3: Your own picture — the sides differ by no more than {pinMaxAspect} times.
question.pin.points.0: Inside the first circle — the full value; beyond it the points fall evenly to zero at the second circle.
question.pin.points.1: The radii are a percentage of the map's longer side.
question.pin.points.2: An answer that earned at least half the value counts as correct: it goes into the streak, accuracy and achievements; less than half is partial.
question.pin.points.3: On the board the share always applies, the “partly” rule isn't needed.
question.pin.points.4: The speed bonus works in classic rounds if it's turned on.
question.pin.tip.0: For cities use the Ukraine or Europe map: on the World map hitting a city is nearly impossible — make the circles bigger.
question.pin.tip.1: Your own picture works for diagrams, paintings, crowd photos (“Where's Wally?”).
question.pin.tip.2: The built-in maps are Natural Earth, public domain; the borders are as Ukraine sees them.
question.pin.title: Pin on the map
question.pin.what: The player places a pin on a map or picture; the closer to the correct one, the more points.
question.poll.how.0: Players pick one option; one vote each.
question.poll.how.1: During the question the stage shows how many have voted; after “Show results” — bars with percentages.
question.poll.how.2: On the console the bars are visible live.
question.poll.limits.2: Buffs don't work; debuffs bought by rivals wait for the next question with points.
question.poll.limits.3: In a team game everyone votes individually, not the captain for the team; no points.
question.poll.points.0: No points. A poll doesn't affect the table, streaks, accuracy or achievements; it doesn't break a streak.
question.poll.tip.0: A good warm-up at the start or a breather between hard rounds.
question.poll.tip.1: You can give the options pictures.
question.poll.title: Poll
question.poll.what: Options with no correct one: find out what the room thinks.
question.single.how.0: The player taps an option — and the answer is sent.
question.single.how.1: An option can be text, a picture or both.
question.single.how.2: With the round setting “Shuffle answer options”, the options come in random order.
question.single.points.0: Correct — the question's value, wrong — 0 (or minus with the penalty).
question.single.tip.0: 3–4 plausible options is the best choice.
question.single.title: One correct option
question.single.what: Several options, one of them correct.
question.slider.how.0: You set the minimum, maximum, step, correct value, unit (optional), tolerance and, if you like, a zero limit.
question.slider.how.1: The player drags the slider (or presses “−” and “+” for one step), sees a big number and confirms with the “Answer” button.
question.slider.how.2: At the reveal the stage shows the scale with every player's mark and the correct value.
question.slider.limits.0: In a blitz, on a blitz cell and in the final, only a hit within the tolerance counts.
question.slider.points.0: Within the tolerance — the full value.
question.slider.points.1: Zero limit: further than ±N from the correct value — 0 points, between the tolerance and the zero limit the points fall evenly. With no zero limit — only the full value or 0.
question.slider.points.2: An answer that earned at least half the value counts as correct: it goes into the streak, the profile accuracy and achievements. Less than half is partial.
question.slider.points.3: On the board the share always applies, the “partly” rule isn't needed here.
question.slider.tip.0: Don't make the range too wide relative to the step: the “−” and “+” buttons give fine tuning, but it shouldn't take many presses.
question.slider.title: Slider
question.slider.what: The answer is a number on a scale: the player drags the slider to their number.
question.sort.how.0: The categories are at the edges of the phone screen, the words come one at a time. The player drags the card, taps a category or presses an arrow.
question.sort.how.1: After a mistake the word goes to the end of the queue and the player's screen “freezes” for the set number of seconds.
question.sort.how.2: On the board whoever picked the cell sorts alone, and the stage and the other phones see their card, where they drag it, its flight and the columns filling up. A mistake — the card shakes red, and the freeze countdown is visible.
question.sort.how.3: While the player drags a card where others can see it, the host sees “→ category” in their row in “Live answers” — where the card is being dragged right now.
question.sort.how.4: In classic rounds, blitzes and the final everyone sorts at the same time: no one sees anyone else's card or movement, the stage only shows progress rows.
question.sort.how.5: At the reveal the words stand in the correct columns: “✗2” means there were two mistakes on this word, a faded “too late” means the word was never reached. In classic rounds everyone sees their own marks on their phone, the stage shows none.
question.sort.limits.2: On the board — only a normal cell answered by phone.
question.sort.points.0: Points for each correctly sorted word.
question.sort.points.1: In a blitz only the first to sort all the words gets points; in the final all the words give plus the stake, and unsorted ones cost minus the stake.
question.sort.points.2: On the board only whoever picked the cell sorts: words × points per word × the cell's mark × the round multiplier, with no minus.
question.sort.tip.0: The total (words × points per word) is no more than {maxPoints}.
question.sort.title: Sorting
question.sort.what: The words have to be sorted into categories.
question.survey.how.0: You set the question and a board of {minSurveyRows}–{maxSurveyRows} rows. Each row has a popularity — how many people out of {surveyTotal} gave this answer (no more than {surveyTotal} in total) — and extra spellings.
question.survey.how.1: If people could choose several answers in the real poll, turn on “The poll allowed more than one answer”: then the total can be over {surveyTotal}, and the share of the value is counted from the total of the whole board — guessing all rows gives the full value.
question.survey.how.2: The player enters up to {maxSurveyAnswers} answers (exactly how many is up to you, {defaultSurveyAnswers} by default) and presses “Answer”.
question.survey.how.3: An answer matches a row ignoring case, extra spaces and the type of apostrophe; the same row doesn't count twice.
question.survey.how.4: The board can be built from a “word cloud” already played in this game: choose “Answers from the cloud” and the cloud you want — up to 8 of the most frequent words, excluding hidden ones, popularity is counted from those who wrote.
question.survey.how.5: If the cloud is empty, the spare board (at least {minSurveyRows} rows) that you added in advance is used; without it the question is skipped, and the console will warn you.
question.survey.how.6: At the reveal the rows open one by one from bottom to top with the host's button, and next to each you can see who named it; “Reveal all” opens the rest at once. Rows that no one named are revealed too.
question.survey.how.7: On the phone a matched answer becomes visible when its row is revealed; misses, points and the verdict — when the whole board is revealed.
question.survey.limits.0: Only classic rounds and a normal board cell answered by phone; a board from a cloud — only in classic rounds.
question.survey.limits.1: The “Double points”, “Extra time”, “Shield”, “Host's hint” and “Swap question” buffs work; 50/50, “Second try” and “Ask the room” don't.
question.survey.limits.2: {minSurveyRows}–{maxSurveyRows} answers on the board, up to {surveyRowText} characters; a player's answer — up to {surveyAnswer}.
question.survey.limits.3: 1–{maxSurveyAnswers} answers per player, {defaultSurveyAnswers} by default. No out-loud cell.
question.survey.limits.4: No emerging picture; video, audio and a picture are fine.
question.survey.points.0: Each answer that matches a row earns points: value × popularity / 100. The same row doesn't count twice; a player can't get more than the value.
question.survey.points.1: Half the value or more counts as a correct answer: it goes into the streak, accuracy and achievements.
question.survey.points.2: The “minus” penalty only hits those who answered and scored no points. On the board the player whose turn it is also gets the minus if they stay silent.
question.survey.points.3: There's no speed bonus. On the board — the cell's value × the mark × the round multiplier.
question.survey.tip.0: Add the usual spellings (“the Beatles” for “Beatles”): a player doesn't lose points over a trifle, and there's no “accept another spelling” during the game.
question.survey.tip.1: Make a board with varied popularity: a very popular row gives lots of points for one word.
question.survey.title: 100 to 1
question.survey.what: A poll of “a hundred people”: players guess the most popular answers, and the stage reveals the board, like on the TV show.
question.text.how.0: The player types the text and presses “Answer”.
question.text.how.1: The answer is compared with all accepted spellings, ignoring case and extra spaces.
question.text.how.2: Accept a correct answer with a different spelling by hand at the reveal.
question.text.points.0: A match with one of the spellings — the question's value, otherwise 0.
question.text.title: Text answer
question.text.what: The player writes the answer themselves.
question.wall.how.0: You set 4 groups of 4 tiles (4×4) or 3 groups of 3 (3×3) and name the link of each group, plus the mistake limit (3 by default).
question.wall.how.1: Players see the same tiles, shuffled so that no row is a ready-made group.
question.wall.how.2: The player selects 4 (or 3) tiles and presses “Check”: a correct group is coloured and locked in place, a wrong one is a mistake. The same wrong selection doesn't count twice.
question.wall.how.3: When one group is left, it solves itself. After the mistake limit, the wall locks for that player.
question.wall.how.4: Players don't see the group names until the reveal: at the reveal the stage shows the groups with names and a table of how many groups each found (up to 14 rows and “+K more”). You see the groups and the players' progress live.
question.wall.how.5: The difference from sorting: there the categories are known, here they have to be guessed.
question.wall.limits.0: Only classic rounds and a normal board cell answered by phone.
question.wall.limits.1: Buffs don't work on the wall.
question.wall.limits.2: The mistake limit is {minWallMistakes}–{maxWallMistakes}, {defaultWallMistakes} by default. A group name is up to {wallGroupName} characters.
question.wall.limits.3: No video; audio and a picture are fine.
question.wall.points.0: Each group found — value / number of groups. The last group solves itself and gives no points: the whole 4×4 wall is worth 75% of the value, 3×3 — 67%.
question.wall.points.1: Half the value or more counts as a correct answer (for 4×4 — from two groups): it goes into the streak, accuracy and achievements.
question.wall.points.2: The “minus” penalty only hits those who tried and found no group at all.
question.wall.points.3: There's no speed bonus. On the board — the cell's value × the mark × the round multiplier.
question.wall.tip.0: Add a “trap”: a word that fits two groups. That makes the wall interesting.
question.wall.tip.1: Raise the value: for the whole wall a player gets no more than three quarters.
question.wall.tip.2: A tile is up to {wallTile} characters: on the phone there are four in a row.
question.wall.title: Connection wall
question.wall.what: The tiles have to be sorted into groups with a common link; the players have to guess the links themselves.
question.wordcloud.how.0: You set the number of words per player (1–{maxCloudWords}).
question.wordcloud.how.1: Identical words are merged ignoring case, extra spaces and the type of apostrophe.
question.wordcloud.how.2: One word from one player counts once.
question.wordcloud.how.3: The console sees the cloud live, along with the authors.
question.wordcloud.how.4: Tap a word to hide it from the screen, tap again to bring it back. A hidden word doesn't reach the stage and stays hidden in the history.
question.wordcloud.how.5: The stage shows the cloud after “Show results” — without hidden words, up to {cloudShown} of the most frequent.
question.wordcloud.limits.2: Buffs don't work; debuffs wait for the next question with points.
question.wordcloud.limits.3: In a team game everyone writes words individually, not the captain for the team; popularity is counted by people.
question.wordcloud.points.0: No points; the cloud doesn't affect the table, streaks, accuracy or achievements.
question.wordcloud.tip.0: An association question (“what do you associate … with”) makes the best cloud.
question.wordcloud.tip.1: A cloud that's been played can be used as a “100 to 1” board later in the game.
question.wordcloud.title: Word cloud
question.wordcloud.what: Each player writes up to three short words, and the stage makes a cloud of them: the more often a word comes up, the bigger it is.
question.wordladder.how.0: Players see the start and target words, the number of letters and the maximum number of steps. The host's path stays hidden until the reveal.
question.wordladder.how.1: Each step is a word with exactly one letter changed, and it must be a noun in the singular nominative. Capitals and the kind of apostrophe don't matter.
question.wordladder.how.2: “Step back” removes the last word. Once the target is reached the result is recorded and can no longer be changed. The stage shows only the number of steps and “finished”; the words appear at the reveal.
question.wordladder.limits.1: Only in a classic round and in the final.
question.wordladder.points.0: The best result in the room counts: whoever got there in the fewest steps gets the full value. Each extra step takes off an equal share: with a value of 500, a best result of 4 steps and a maximum of 8 you get 500, 400, 300, 200, 100 for 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8 steps.
question.wordladder.points.1: Whoever took more steps than the maximum, or never got there — 0. If nobody got there, everyone gets zero. Speed, partial credit and buffs do not apply; the round multiplier does.
question.wordladder.points.2: In the final the ladder is “correct” if the player got there in no more than the maximum number of steps: plus the stake, and for everyone else minus the stake.
question.wordladder.tip.0: Check the path out loud: every word must be a noun, and neighbouring words must differ by one letter.
question.wordladder.title: Word ladder
question.wordladder.what: A ladder from one word to another: one letter changes each time, and every word is a noun.
round.auction.how.0: Each question is preceded by bidding. The stage shows only the start of the text (the number of words is set in the editor) and the question price, without options or media. Players bid on their phones and outbid each other; everyone sees the highest bid and who made it.
round.auction.how.1: A clock closes the bidding: there are 15 s for the first bid, and after every bid the countdown starts over — 5 more seconds.
round.auction.how.2: You can close the bidding earlier with the “Sold” button: the question opens for the winner.
round.auction.how.3: Only the winner of the bidding answers, the others watch. If nobody bids, the question is a normal one and everyone answers.
round.auction.limits.0: A bid cannot exceed the player’s own points; with 0 points a player does not take part in the bidding.
round.auction.limits.1: The same question types as in the final.
round.auction.limits.2: No buffs, no debuff shop and no “Undo”.
round.auction.points.0: The winner answers correctly: they get the question price and their bid.
round.auction.points.1: The winner is wrong or silent: they lose the bid (or the bid and the question price — set in the round settings).
round.auction.points.2: Nobody bid: a normal question, the price for a correct answer, no speed bonus.
round.auction.tip.0: Cut the text at a word that does not give the answer away yet, and set a price worth outbidding.
round.auction.title: Auction
round.auction.what: A round with open bidding before each question: only the theme and the price are visible, and whoever bids the most answers.
round.bets.how.0: Before every question players place a secret bet on their phone. The stage shows only the start of the question (the number of words is set in the editor), with no options or media.
round.bets.how.1: The question opens when everyone who can has bet, or when you press “Open question”. A bet can be changed until it opens.
round.bets.how.2: Anyone who hasn't bet or can't afford the minimum skips this question: no answer and no points.
round.bets.how.3: After the question closes the reveal is immediate for everyone: the stage shows each player's bet, result and points.
round.bets.limits.0: The last question's minimum bet is no more than the maximum; bets up to {maxBet}.
round.bets.limits.1: The same question types as in the final.
round.bets.limits.3: The maximum bet is optional: if it is not set, a player can bet all their points. A bet can never exceed the player's points.
round.bets.points.0: Whoever answers correctly keeps their bet and shares the bank (the bets of those who were wrong or didn't answer) in proportion to the bets.
round.bets.points.1: If nobody answers correctly, all bets are returned.
round.bets.points.2: No question price, round rules, speed bonus or buffs here.
round.bets.tip.0: Cut the text at a word that doesn't give the answer away yet: a bet should be a risk, not a certainty.
round.bets.title: Bets
round.bets.what: A round with secret bets before every question: only the start of the text is visible, and the minimum bet grows with each question.
round.blitz.how.0: “Host” checking: players press “Answer” on their phone and join the queue. The first in the queue answers (within the answer window, if one is set), and you judge “Correct” or “Wrong”. While you decide, the timer stops.
round.blitz.how.1: After a mistake the next in the queue answers. Each player has as many tries as set in the round settings.
round.blitz.how.2: “Automatic” checking is an instant blitz: there's no button, everyone answers once straight away. Answers queue up by time, you press “Accept answer” in turn, and correctness is checked automatically.
round.blitz.how.3: The question closes after the first correct answer, when time runs out or when everyone has run out of tries.
round.blitz.limits.0: In a team game anyone on the team can press, and whoever pressed answers; the team shares its tries.
round.blitz.limits.1: There are no word chains in a blitz.
round.blitz.limits.2: “Who am I?” and pin on the map aren't available here.
round.blitz.limits.3: Buffs don't work in a blitz.
round.blitz.limits.4: Connection walls, polls, word clouds and “100 to 1” aren't available here.
round.blitz.points.0: The first to answer correctly gets the question's value (× the round multiplier), everyone else gets 0.
round.blitz.points.1: With the “minus” penalty, each wrong try takes away the question's value (except for sorting).
round.blitz.points.2: There's no speed bonus and no “partly” in a blitz.
round.blitz.points.3: Sorting in a blitz is won by whoever sorts all the words first.
round.blitz.points.4: Without an answer window and without a timer, the answer is still given {defaultAnswerWindow} seconds.
round.blitz.tip.0: An instant blitz is handy for a big group: you don't have to judge everyone by hand.
round.blitz.tip.1: Manual checking suits answers in players' own words.
round.blitz.title: Blitz
round.blitz.what: Questions for the quickest: only the first to answer correctly gets points.
round.board.how.0: On the round intro, set the order: “Roll the dice” (everyone rolls on their phone), with the arrows or “In joining order”.
round.board.how.1: On their turn a player taps a cell on their phone, or you pick for them on the console. The cell flips over and everyone sees the question.
round.board.how.2: On a normal cell only whoever picked it answers — by phone or out loud. The others watch.
round.board.how.3: An answer from the phone comes to you. With automatic checking you press “Accept answer” or “Pick again” (the player answers once more, the time keeps running). With manual checking you mark it yourself.
round.board.how.4: If the player whose turn it is goes offline, the turn is skipped after 30 seconds; “Skip turn” skips it at once.
round.board.how.5: The round ends when all the cells have been played or you press “End round”.
round.board.limits.0: {minCategories}–{maxCategories} categories, each with {minCategoryQuestions}–{maxCategoryQuestions} cells, up to {maxBoardCells} cells on the board.
round.board.limits.1: There are no word chains on the board; sorting and connection walls only on a normal cell answered by phone.
round.board.limits.2: Polls and word clouds aren't available: on the board one player answers.
round.board.limits.3: “100 to 1” only with the host's board (from a cloud — in classic rounds).
round.board.limits.5: In a team game the teams take turns in a circle: the captain picks the cell and answers, and on an out-loud cell anyone on the team answers out loud and you mark the team's result.
round.board.points.0: A correct answer earns the cell's value × the mark (×2/×3) × the round multiplier.
round.board.points.1: With the “minus” penalty, a mistake or silence on a normal cell takes away the same amount.
round.board.points.2: There's no speed bonus. Partial points (ordering, a number with a deviation, the “Partly” mark) only come with the “partly” rule, otherwise a nearly correct answer gives 0.
round.board.points.3: Sorting on the board: words × points per word × the cell's mark × the round multiplier, with no minus and no partial points for progress.
round.board.points.4: A streak only counts the player's own cells.
round.board.tip.0: Put cheap cells at the top and expensive ones at the bottom — that makes it easier for players to choose their risk.
round.board.tip.1: One or two hidden ×2 cells and one blitz cell make the board come alive.
round.board.tip.2: For “Swap question”, add 1–2 spares to each category.
round.board.tip.3: In the editor a cell with ✓ is ready, with ! — incomplete, a dashed one — empty; above each column you can see how many are ready. “Save” checks the same thing.
round.board.title: Game board
round.board.what: A board with categories and values: players take turns picking a cell, and whoever picked it answers.
round.classic.how.0: You press “Start round” — the question appears on the stage and on the phones, and the timer runs.
round.classic.how.1: The question closes when everyone has answered, the time runs out or you press “Close question”.
round.classic.how.2: “Show answer”: the stage shows the correct answer, the phones show the result and points. Here you can accept or reject a player's answer by hand.
round.classic.how.3: If the leaderboard is shown after every question, the table comes next, then the next question.
round.classic.limits.0: Polls and word clouds only exist here: they give no points and don't change the table.
round.classic.limits.1: In a team game the captain answers; everyone does polls and clouds individually.
round.classic.points.0: Everyone who answers correctly gets the question's value.
round.classic.points.1: With the speed bonus, an instant answer gets the full value and an answer in the last second gets half. Questions with video and emerging pictures have no speed bonus.
round.classic.points.2: Ordering and numbers with a deviation give part of the value for a nearly correct answer.
round.classic.points.3: The “minus” penalty, “partly”, streaks and the multiplier are set in the round settings (see their “ⓘ”).
round.classic.points.4: On equal points, whoever answered faster in classic rounds ranks higher.
round.classic.tip.0: Bluff works best in classic rounds: everyone makes things up and picks together.
round.classic.tip.1: A themed or music round is just a normal round where all questions are of one kind (for example, all with audio).
round.classic.tip.2: A geography round is a normal round where all questions are “Pin on the map”.
round.classic.tip.3: For a warm-up, turn off the penalty and give 20–30 seconds per question.
round.classic.tip.4: A poll or word cloud at the start is a good way to warm up the room (no points).
round.classic.tip.5: “100 to 1” from a word cloud: first the cloud, then a board made of the players' own answers.
round.classic.tip.6: “All in” is a separate round type for tension at the end of the game.
round.classic.tip.7: “Knockout” is a separate round type where a mistake threatens elimination.
round.classic.title: Classic
round.classic.what: Ordinary questions one after another: all players answer at the same time, each on their own phone.
round.final.how.0: After the intro, players place a stake on their phone — from 0 up to their score; “All in” stakes everything. Anyone with 0 or less can only stake 0.
round.final.how.1: The question opens when everyone has staked, or when you press “Show question”.
round.final.how.2: Everyone answers at the same time. With manual checking you judge each answer: “Accept” or “Don't count”.
round.final.how.3: At the reveal, players are shown one by one (“Next player”): the stage shows the stake and the new score. With a shared bank the last step is “Split the bank”.
round.final.limits.0: In a team game there's one stake per team from the team's points: the captain stakes and answers.
round.final.limits.2: “Who am I?” and pin on the map aren't available here.
round.final.limits.3: Debuffs can't be bought in the final round.
round.final.limits.4: Connection walls, polls, word clouds and “100 to 1” aren't available here.
round.final.points.0: Classic stakes: a correct answer — plus the stake, a wrong one or none — minus the stake.
round.final.points.1: Shared bank: whoever got it wrong or stayed silent gives their stake to the bank; whoever answered correctly keeps theirs and shares the bank in proportion to the stakes. If no one with a stake is correct, the stakes are returned.
round.final.points.2: There are no partial points: only correct (+stake) or wrong (−stake).
round.final.points.3: The final has no question value, round rules, speed bonus or buffs.
round.final.tip.0: Make the final the last round — then the stakes make sense.
round.final.tip.1: A shared bank rescues those who are behind: a careful stake loses nothing.
round.final.tip.2: The “All in” button in stakes isn't the same as the “All in” round.
round.final.title: Final
round.final.what: One question for everyone with stakes: each player secretly stakes part of their points.
round.ladder.how.0: On the round intro, pick the contestant on the console. With a draw or “fewest points”, press “Pick a contestant” — the stage will show who's going. The contestant can be changed before the first question.
round.ladder.how.1: The contestant answers the questions in turn; the stage and all phones see the questions. The stage shows the contestant's final answer as soon as the question closes.
round.ladder.how.2: After “Show answer” and “Next”, the stage shows the ladder. If the answer is correct, the contestant chooses “Play on” or “Take” on their phone. If they decided out loud or dropped offline, decide for them on the console.
round.ladder.how.3: A wrong answer or silence ends the ladder, and the contestant gets the amount of the last safe step passed (or nothing). A correct answer to the last question gives the top amount.
round.ladder.how.4: Lifelines: 50/50 removes two wrong options (everyone sees it); “Room” — the percentages of the room's answers (voting lasts 15 s or closes when everyone or the contestant has answered; until then the others only see a counter; whoever didn't make it can no longer answer this question); “Host's hint” — text from the editor or your hint from the console. Each once per ladder, several can be used on one question.
round.ladder.how.5: A timer per question is optional; without it the contestant thinks as long as needed, and you close the question.
round.ladder.how.6: If you end the round mid-ladder, the contestant takes what they've already climbed.
round.ladder.limits.0: {minLadderQuestions}–{maxLadderQuestions} “single choice” questions, each with exactly {ladderOptions} options.
round.ladder.limits.1: Step amounts rise from bottom to top, up to {maxLadderLevel}; the top one can't be safe.
round.ladder.limits.2: Quiz buffs, debuffs (from the host and from the shop) and duels don't work in this round; a waiting debuff and a duel declared earlier happen after the round.
round.ladder.limits.3: There are no round rules: no multiplier, no minus, no streaks, no speed bonus.
round.ladder.limits.4: Between questions the stage shows the ladder, not the table; the “Table” button on the phone works.
round.ladder.limits.5: There's one contestant per round, and they can't be changed after the first question.
round.ladder.limits.6: In a team game a team becomes the contestant, the captain answers and decides, and the room is the other teams: their captains answer for themselves.
round.ladder.points.0: The contestant wins the level's amount, not the sum of the questions: up to {maxLadderLevel} points. The winnings are added as one “Ladder winnings” line.
round.ladder.points.1: The contestant's answers count towards accuracy but give no points by themselves.
round.ladder.points.2: The room gets 10% of the level's amount for each correct answer; this doesn't affect the contestant. The room's silence doesn't spoil accuracy.
round.ladder.tip.0: Want several contestants? Add several “Millionaire” rounds (for example, with the “fewest points” pick).
round.ladder.tip.1: Put safe steps at one third and two thirds of the ladder — that way the risk is real but not ruinous.
round.ladder.tip.2: Write the hint into the question — then “Host's hint” won't distract you mid-game.
round.ladder.title: Millionaire
round.ladder.what: One contestant climbs a ladder of four-option questions: each correct answer is a step up, and before each next question they can take the money. Everyone else is the room: they answer for themselves and get 10% of the level's amount.
round.survival.how.0: Everyone still alive answers the question at the same time, and points are counted by the round rules: multiplier, penalty, partial points, streaks, speed bonus.
round.survival.how.1: Whoever got it wrong or didn't answer (including dropping offline) goes “on the edge”. If all the living ended up on the edge (everyone present is on the edge), no one is knocked out and there's no trial.
round.survival.how.2: After “Show answer” you press “Next”: those “on the edge” face a trial. There are two kinds, and you choose in the round settings.
round.survival.how.3: “Survival question” — one spare question of the round for everyone “on the edge” at once: a mistake or silence — you're out. When these questions run out, the trial becomes “Luck”.
round.survival.how.4: “Luck” — everyone “on the edge” picks one of three doors; behind one (different for each, at random) is a trap, and whoever picks it is out. If you don't choose within {survivalLuckSeconds} s, a door is picked for you.
round.survival.how.5: The trial closes as soon as everyone “on the edge” has answered, when time runs out or when you press “Close the trial”. Pause stops the countdown.
round.survival.how.6: A text answer to a survival question can be accepted or rejected by hand while the trial is closed and the result is on the stage; after “Next” it can't.
round.survival.how.7: Ghosts see the question and answer “for themselves”: this gives no points, streaks or achievements, and the stage shows how many ghosts got it.
round.survival.how.8: The round ends when, after a knockout, no more remain than you set (one player by default), or when the questions run out. Everyone who survives gets the survival bonus.
round.survival.limits.0: {minSurvivalQuestions}–{maxSurvivalQuestions} questions and up to {maxSurvivalTrials} survival questions: single choice, yes/no, number, text, slider. Survival questions have no video, audio or emerging picture.
round.survival.limits.1: How many should remain — from 1 to {maxSurvivors}. If there are no more players than that from the start, the round goes on until the questions run out. If this number is no less than the number of players, the round ends with the very first knockout.
round.survival.limits.2: There are no buffs in this round. Debuffs (both from the host and from the shop) work, but only on the living; a ghost can buy debuffs and cast them on the living.
round.survival.limits.3: There are no duels in this round: a duel declared earlier takes place after the round, but only if the duel cut-off hasn't passed yet; after the cut-off, duels no longer happen.
round.survival.limits.4: Between questions the stage shows the “alive and ghosts” page, not the table; the “Table” button on the phone works.
round.survival.limits.5: Ending the round mid-question works as in a classic round, with no trial; mid-trial, the trial closes as if time ran out.
round.survival.limits.6: In a team game a team counts as one player: the captain does the answers, trials and doors; a ghost team also answers “for themselves” through the captain.
round.survival.points.0: Points per question work as in a classic round: the question's value, multiplier, penalty, partial points, streaks and speed bonus, if turned on.
round.survival.points.1: The survival bonus is a set number of points for everyone who survives to the end of the round; it appears as a separate adjustment line.
round.survival.points.2: Survival questions and luck give no points: they only decide who stays.
round.survival.points.3: A correct answer means “fully correct”: a partial one or a slider below half the value counts as a mistake.
round.survival.tip.0: Add enough survival questions: a question is fairer, luck is more fun. When the questions run out, the trial becomes luck.
round.survival.tip.1: Make the first questions easier so no one is knocked out too early.
round.survival.tip.2: Make the survival bonus worth it, otherwise a knockout costs nothing.
round.survival.title: Knockout
round.survival.what: Points work as in a classic round, but whoever gets it wrong or stays silent goes “on the edge” and faces a trial. Whoever fails it is knocked out: they become a ghost and from then on play just for themselves.
round.wipeout.how.0: Everyone still in the game gets the same question at the same time.
round.wipeout.how.1: During the question the stage shows the banks of everyone in the game at the side, and the phones show an “In the game: …” strip. After “Show answer” the stage and phones see who answered correctly and how their bank grew, and who burned. Whoever got it wrong or didn't answer (including dropping offline) burns: bank 0, and they only watch until the end of the round.
round.wipeout.how.2: You press “Next” — the ladder is on the stage, and players still in the game choose “Next” or “Take” on their phone. They have up to {wipeoutDecideSeconds} seconds (the window closes early once everyone has decided); whoever doesn't choose takes the bank automatically. Players don't see others' decisions until the window closes, but you see them live. As soon as the window closes, the stage, phones and console show the “Decisions” screen: who took the bank, who goes on, and who didn't choose and had the bank taken for them (“No choice”). If “Minimum time before “Next”” is on, “Next” on that screen works no sooner than after {paceDecisions} s.
round.wipeout.how.3: While players are deciding, the “Next” button on the console waits. Pause stops the countdown.
round.wipeout.how.4: If you end the round while a question's intro is playing, the question doesn't count and the banks stay; during the decision window, those who haven't decided take their bank.
round.wipeout.how.5: After the last question, the banks of the survivors go into their points automatically. If no one is left in the game, the round ends early.
round.wipeout.how.6: Only a text answer can be accepted or rejected by hand (“Accept” / “Reject”, no “Partly”), while the answer is on the stage (before “Next”); the verdict changes the bank and the player's fate at once. Other answer types aren't judged by hand.
round.wipeout.limits.0: {minWipeoutQuestions}–{maxWipeoutQuestions} questions: single choice, yes/no, number, text, slider.
round.wipeout.limits.1: Buffs, debuffs (both from the host and from the shop) and duels don't work in this round; a waiting debuff kicks in in the next round.
round.wipeout.limits.2: Between questions the stage shows the ladder, not the table; the “Table” button on the phone works.
round.wipeout.limits.3: The bank can only be taken after a correct answer; before the first question there's nothing to take.
round.wipeout.limits.4: Ending the round mid-question is like time running out: whoever didn't answer in time burns.
round.wipeout.limits.5: In a team game a team counts as one player: the captain submits the answers and the “take or go on” decisions.
round.wipeout.points.0: Points come only from a bank that was taken or carried to the end: the sum of the values of the questions the player answered correctly.
round.wipeout.points.1: A burned bank gives nothing, but doesn't take away the game points already earned either.
round.wipeout.points.2: Numbers and sliders only count within the tolerance: there are no partial points here.
round.wipeout.points.3: “All in” has no multiplier, penalty, streaks or speed bonus.
round.wipeout.tip.0: Use rising values: 100, 200, 300… Then the last steps are truly tempting.
round.wipeout.tip.1: Make the first questions easy so the bank can build up; the last ones hard.
round.wipeout.tip.2: Don't confuse it with the “All in” button in the final's stakes: there the whole score is staked on one question.
round.wipeout.tip.3: A similar ladder for one player is the “Millionaire” round.
round.wipeout.title: All in
round.wipeout.what: A ladder of questions: a correct answer adds the value to the bank, a mistake burns it. After each correct one, the player decides — risk going on or take the bank into their points.
setting.appeal.how.0: At the reveal of a classic question or a normal board cell, whoever's answer was judged wrong or partial sees “⚖️ Appeal (2 left)” on their phone. In a team game the captain appeals.
setting.appeal.how.1: Only those who are connected vote, except the person appealing and their team: in a team game — people from other teams, each person individually. Voting lasts {appealVote} s or closes as soon as everyone has voted. A vote can be changed until the end.
setting.appeal.how.2: On the stage and the phones — the card “Olya appeals: the answer “…”, the correct one is “…”. Accept it?”, a counter “yes 3 · no 1 · 2 still thinking” and a countdown. No one sees whose votes they are — not even you: only the counters.
setting.appeal.how.3: While the room votes, “Next” is inactive: the button says “The room is voting”. Pause stops the countdown. “End round”, “End game” and removing a player work at once.
setting.appeal.how.4: The second ground is the penalty for leaving the game (12e): if there's going to be a penalty for the question, the player can appeal it: “⚖️ Appeal the penalty”. It's the same appeal and the same limit. The room lifts the penalty on an out-loud board cell too.
setting.appeal.limits.0: Blitz, final, “All in”, “Knockout”, “Millionaire” and duels can't be appealed. Where even the host doesn't change the judgement (chain, sorting, wall, “100 to 1”, bluff, poll, cloud), it can't be appealed either.
setting.appeal.limits.1: An out-loud answer on a board cell can't be appealed on its judgement: the room has nothing to see.
setting.appeal.limits.2: If there's no one to vote, there's no button: the phone says “No one to vote”.
setting.appeal.limits.3: In a game without a host this is the only way to lift the leaving penalty: the reveal lasts at least {autopilotAppealWindow} s while someone can still appeal, and after the decision — another {autopilotAppealShown} s.
setting.appeal.points.0: The decision is a simple majority: more “yes” than “no”. Then a separate “appeal” line gives as much as a “Correct” judgement would have, and the leaving penalty isn't applied. A draw or no votes at all — everything stays as it was. The answer's verdict and streaks don't change.
setting.appeal.points.1: The limit is {appealsPerGame} appeals per game per player or team; one the room rejected counts too.
setting.appeal.tip.0: You have no right of veto. But if you agree with the player yourself, press “Correct” while the vote is still on: the appeal is closed with the note “Accepted by the host”, and it doesn't count towards the limit. This applies to judgements, not to the leaving penalty.
setting.appeal.tip.1: The room's decision is undone in the “↶ Points” sheet after moving on, like any row: “Olya +150 (appeal)”. After a won appeal the judgement can't be changed at the same reveal. While there's a leaving penalty on this question, undo the penalty first. After the game ends, appeal decisions can't be undone, only penalties.
setting.appeal.title: Appeal
setting.appeal.what: A player whose answer wasn't accepted or who lost points for leaving the game asks the room: 30 seconds of voting, and the room decides without the host.
setting.audio.how.0: The sound plays on the stage after the question's intro. A stage opened late plays only the rest of the clip; a clip that has already finished doesn't repeat by itself.
setting.audio.how.1: The console plays the sound itself only if the stage isn't open or has dropped out for about 3 s. Phones don't play the sound.
setting.audio.how.2: The console has “Play again” and “Stop” buttons; pausing the game pauses the sound.
setting.audio.how.3: If the clip is shorter than the question's time, the timer runs alongside the sound; if longer, the timer starts after the clip, and the board shows “🎵 Listen”.
setting.audio.how.4: The browser may not allow sound without a tap: then a “🔊 Turn on sound” button appears on the stage — one tap.
setting.audio.limits.0: MP3, OGG or M4A up to {audioMaxMb} MB.
setting.audio.limits.2: Not together with a normal video; not in spare questions.
setting.audio.points.0: Doesn't affect points; the speed bonus is counted from the whole time including the sound.
setting.audio.tip.0: A music round is a normal round where all questions have audio.
setting.audio.tip.1: A clip of 5–15 seconds is enough to recognise a song.
setting.audio.tip.2: YouTube “sound only” hides the picture and the video's title.
setting.audio.title: Audio for the question
setting.audio.what: Sound for a question of any type: an uploaded file or YouTube “sound only”.
setting.autopilot.how.0: Launch: “Run with the bot” in the quiz list → the changes that will be needed → “Create room”. You're on your phone as a player; in the lobby — the code, a QR, a link to the stage and “Start game”.
setting.autopilot.how.1: The bot opens and closes questions, reveals answers, shows the table and moves on by itself. It rolls the dice for those who haven't (board — after {autopilotBoardDice} s, teams — after {autopilotTeamDice} s); skips turns on the board, picks the duel category, holds the “Millionaire” draw, “Takes” the money if there's no decision within {autopilotLadderDecision} s, and puts together teams set to “I'll split them myself” at random at the start.
setting.autopilot.how.2: Stage timings: “How to play” — {autopilotGuide} s; round intro — {autopilotIntro} s plus {autopilotIntroPerChars} s for every {autopilotIntroChars} characters of description, but no more than {autopilotIntroMax} s; from closing to reveal — {autopilotLocked} s; reveal — {autopilotReveal} s (at least {autopilotAppealWindow} s while someone can still appeal; the bot waits for an appeal vote, and after the decision — another {autopilotAppealShown} s); a “100 to 1” row or bluff option — {autopilotRow} s, after the last one another {autopilotRowsTail} s; table — {autopilotLeaderboard} s; “All in” decisions — {autopilotDecisions} s; end of round — {autopilotRoundEnd} s; in the final, each player — {autopilotFinalRow} s. It's never less than the 11b minimum time.
setting.autopilot.how.3: The launch window lists by round what changes in the formats: “out loud” answers are typed on the phone, the key replaces manual checking, a draw picks the “Millionaire” contestant, the hint only works with text in the question, questions without a timer close after their own time.
setting.autopilot.how.4: The author's “⋯” menu: pause and resume, removing a player, ending the game, in a team game's lobby — how we form teams, on a “word cloud” and bluff — “Hide…”. A bluff fib can only be removed after making your own pick.
setting.autopilot.how.5: If no one is connected, the game pauses; as soon as someone comes back, it carries on after {autopilotResume} s. The same after a server restart.
setting.autopilot.how.6: The sound plays on the stage, and when there's no stage, on the players' phones.
setting.autopilot.limits.0: The leaving penalty works without a host too. In a game without a host only an appeal lifts the penalty.
setting.autopilot.limits.1: No judging, no adjusting or undoing points, no debuffs from the host, no “±15 s”, no replaying the sound.
setting.autopilot.limits.2: The “Millionaire” hint is only there when its text is written in the question.
setting.autopilot.limits.3: The answer key replaces manual checking.
setting.autopilot.points.0: The author's result counts like any player's. “Games hosted” and host achievements aren't added for such a game: the game is marked “Run by the bot” in the history.
setting.autopilot.tip.0: Open the stage on the TV via the link from the lobby. You know the answers — play fair.
setting.autopilot.title: Game without a host
setting.autopilot.what: The bot hosts the game: the author plays as a regular player from their phone, and there's no host console.
setting.away.how.0: Leaving the game's tab or app counts from {awayMark} s in total while the person is still answering the question: from the start (after the intro) until their answer or the close. The server counts the time, a pause stops it.
setting.away.how.1: On the console next to the name — “🙈 out of the game 12 s (2 times)”, and while the person is away — “🙈 out of the game for now”. On the stage — only an icon with the names “🙈 Olya, Petro”, without seconds.
setting.away.how.2: When the player who was away comes back, their phone turns red, a siren sounds and it says “🚨 You left the game during a question!”. It can be closed with a tap, otherwise it disappears by itself after {awayAlarm} s. Nothing is shown on other phones. The player also sees their line “You were out of the game for 8 s — the host and the screen can see it”.
setting.away.how.3: An optional penalty (a checkbox in the quiz settings): from {awayPenalty} s in total — 0 points for the question. It works in classic rounds, on the board, in a blitz and in the final; in “All in”, “Knockout”, “Millionaire”, polls and clouds — only the mark.
setting.away.how.4: In a team game the mark and the alarm are next to the person, and the team gets the penalty if any of its connected members was away for {awayPenalty} s or more in total.
setting.away.how.5: During the game the phone doesn't let the screen go dark: the screen doesn't switch off by itself.
