If the browser can't do this or didn't allow it, in a game with the penalty the phone asks you not to let the screen go dark. If the phone was locked already at the start of the question, the first {awayPreGrace} s don't count.
setting.away.limits.0: Leaving while offline counts for no longer than the disconnection lasted: the server takes the smaller of the two — what the phone reported and how long the disconnection was. Networks drop out without anyone googling, too.
setting.away.limits.1: Someone who turns on flight mode first and only then leaves the game goes unnoticed: a phone without a connection doesn't manage to report leaving.
setting.away.limits.2: A second device, a laptop nearby or a neighbour's hint can't be seen. On some phones the notification shade counts as leaving. An old browser sends nothing.
setting.away.limits.3: Leaving interrupted by a server restart may show up as two departures (2 times). This is a known limitation.
setting.away.points.0: Only earned points are taken away: leaving doesn't cancel the minus for a mistake.
setting.away.points.1: The penalty is a separate “left the game” row in the “↶ Points” sheet: undo it with one tap if the player just got a phone call. This can be done even after the game ends; then only the penalty is undone, the other points can no longer change. In a game without a host only an appeal lifts the penalty: the player asks the room, and the room votes.
setting.away.tip.0: Anyone who taps the YouTube logo in a video question ends up on youtube.com — that's leaving the game too.
setting.away.title: Out of the game and the leaving penalty
setting.away.what: The phone notices when a player leaves the game while a question is open: another tab or app, a locked screen, a call.
setting.blitzSeries.how.0: The player sees the streak on the phone and how much the next answer will give; the stage and the console show a mark by the name.
setting.blitzSeries.limits.0: Only in a blitz round; a streak starts from zero in every new round; blitz cells on the board have no streaks.
setting.blitzSeries.points.1: A correct answer resets the minus streak, a mistake resets the plus streak; someone who did not press does not move the streak; every attempt is a separate step.
setting.blitzSeries.points.2: The round multiplier multiplies the price, not the step.
setting.blitzSeries.tip.0: The minus streak makes random guessing a losing move.
setting.blitzSeries.title: Blitz streaks
setting.blitzSeries.what: Each correct answer in a row gives one step more, each wrong answer in a row takes one step more.
setting.debuffShop.how.0: The phone has a “Debuffs” 😈 button: the player picks a debuff and a rival, and the points are deducted at once.
setting.debuffShop.how.1: One purchase between two questions. The rival must be connected to the game and have no other debuff.
setting.debuffShop.how.2: The debuff kicks in on the next question where the rival answers by phone. Everyone sees who attacked whom.
setting.debuffShop.how.3: You cast debuffs for free from the player's row on the console. Your own debuff can be cancelled before it fires, a bought one can't.
setting.debuffShop.how.4: A quiz where debuffs haven't been chosen yet has the first six; the five new ones (Upside down, Torch, Sticky buttons, No clock, Bubbles) are turned on in the editor, under “Buffs and debuffs”.
setting.debuffShop.limits.0: In a team game the captain buys a debuff with team points and casts it on another team.
setting.debuffShop.limits.1: Can't be bought in the final round, in “All in”, in “Millionaire” (the shop is closed), during a pause or during a duel. In “Knockout” it can be bought, but not for ghosts; a ghost can buy for the living.
setting.debuffShop.points.0: The price is set separately for each debuff: from {minDebuffPrice} to {maxDebuffPrice} points, {defaultDebuffPrice} by default.
setting.debuffShop.points.1: You can't go into minus with a purchase.
setting.debuffShop.tip.0: A price of about 20% of a normal question's value makes purchases frequent, a higher one makes them rare and painful.
setting.debuffShop.tip.1: Untick “Players can buy debuffs” so that only you cast debuffs.
setting.debuffShop.title: Debuff shop
setting.debuffShop.what: Players can buy debuffs for rivals with their own points.
setting.description.how.0: Up to {roundDescription} characters; the counter under the field turns yellow when little is left.
setting.description.how.1: The description is shown on the round intro above the rules reminder — on the stage, phones and console.
setting.description.how.2: If it doesn't fit on the stage together with the rules, the stage cuts the description with an ellipsis; the phones and console show it in full.
setting.description.tip.0: Write the most important part first: on the stage it's always visible.
setting.description.title: Round description for players
setting.description.what: Your words for the round: the theme, the mood, special conditions.
setting.duels.how.0: After a third of the questions (not counting the final), “⚔ Duel” appears on the phone. You can challenge until the final or until the last round; the rival can't refuse.
setting.duels.how.1: The duel starts after the current question with a “Duel!” intro. The challenger picks the category (or you do for them).
setting.duels.how.2: Both type answers, with many tries (up to {maxDuelTries}); the first correct one wins the question. You can skip a question or cancel the duel.
setting.duels.limits.0: In a team game a duel is team against team: the captain declares it, the captain picks the duellist on the phone (themselves by default), and only the duellist answers.
setting.duels.limits.1: Answers in a duel are text only.
setting.duels.limits.2: There are no buffs or debuffs in a duel.
setting.duels.limits.3: In “All in”, “Knockout” and “Millionaire” duels aren't declared and don't start; one declared earlier starts after the round, but only if this round comes before the duel cut-off (before the final or before the last round).
setting.duels.points.0: Whoever wins more questions wins and takes the stake from the rival. A draw — points don't change.
setting.duels.tip.0: Each category must have at least as many questions as one duel; more is better — a category can be picked twice.
setting.duels.title: Duels
setting.duels.what: Once per game a player can challenge a rival to a duel on separate questions.
setting.leaderboard.how.0: “After every question”: the leaderboard screen comes after the reveal, and on the board — after every cell.
setting.leaderboard.how.1: “Only at the end of the game”: there's no leaderboard between questions (in “All in” there's always the ladder between questions, and in “Knockout” the “alive / ghosts” page, not the table), but the round results with the full table and the podium stay. In “Millionaire” there's always the ladder between questions. Between round results the “Table” button on the phone shows the player only their own place. The round columns are visible wherever the table is: between results a player sees only their own row and their own breakdown.
setting.leaderboard.points.0: Doesn't affect points. Polls and clouds don't change the table.
setting.leaderboard.tip.0: “Only at the end” keeps the suspense and speeds up the game; “after every” adds a competitive mood.
setting.leaderboard.title: Show the leaderboard
setting.leaderboard.what: When players see the points table.
setting.levelBonuses.how.0: From level 5, “+5 s” appears on the phone (from level 20 — “+10 s”): it adds time for the player on a question. From level 10 — “Level hint”: it shows the hint you wrote for the question.
setting.levelBonuses.how.1: From level 15 the player has “Charm”: it blocks the first debuff against them, yours or a bought one. You see 🛡 next to such a player.
setting.levelBonuses.how.2: Each bonus once per game. It doesn't take a buff's place and doesn't count as a used buff.
setting.levelBonuses.limits.0: Guests and team games don't get bonuses. In a blitz, the final and other special rounds there are no buttons, just as with buffs.
setting.levelBonuses.points.0: A bonus is only given if the quiz has something to use it on: a timer, hints in the questions, allowed debuffs.
setting.levelBonuses.tip.0: Untick “Level bonuses” so that everyone plays on equal terms. The lobby shows whether bonuses are on.
setting.levelBonuses.title: Level bonuses
setting.levelBonuses.what: Players with accounts at level 5+ get small bonuses for the game: “+5 s”, “Level hint” and “Charm”.
setting.live.how.0: The “👁 Live” switch in the console header turns the live picks on and off. On by default; this device remembers the choice. When off, the panel collapses to a “5 of 8 answered” line, and the console gets no live picks at all. The blitz queue with its buttons stays.
setting.live.how.1: Until a player has sent their answer, their row shows the current pick in italics with a “not sent yet” mark: “marking Whale, Dolphin”, “typing “Osaka””, order, pairs, slider, a pin on the mini-map, selected wall tiles, a chain word, a bluff fib, cloud words and “100 to 1”.
setting.live.how.10: The “Accept answer”, “Partly”, “Reject” and “Pick again” buttons stay where they were. After the reveal the panel is replaced by the usual “Answers” with judging.
setting.live.how.2: Next to it — “changed 3 times” and “thinking for 12 s” (since the last change). After “Send” the row shows the submitted answer.
setting.live.how.3: A player sends a single choice (and “Yes / No”, polls) with one tap, so it shows straight away as an answer.
setting.live.how.4: At the top — “5 of 8 answered” and (with “👁 Live” on) “Waiting for: …” chips. A grey chip means the player is offline. Tapping the counter in the phase bar scrolls to the panel.
setting.live.how.5: The row has the answer, time, buff, spare question and the auto-check's preliminary verdict: “correct”, “partly” or “no”. “Awaiting a decision” means the answer is waiting for your “Accept answer” or judgement.
setting.live.how.6: Chains, sorting and walls show progress: how many words are guessed and the current word, the current card and mistakes, groups found. Bluff — the fib, then the pick. “100 to 1” — which board row the answer hit. Blitz — the live queue.
setting.live.how.7: “All in” and “Knockout” only show those still in the game, “Millionaire” — the contestant; ghosts and the room are in a collapsed list under the rows.
setting.live.how.8: The panel is also there during an open “Knockout” trial (who is “on the edge”: a door or an answer with a verdict) and in a duel (each duellist's tries and the winning answer).
setting.live.how.9: In a team game a row is a team: who in it is acting right now and, until there's an answer, the captain's pick in italics (only with “live” on).
setting.live.limits.0: In a game without a host there are no live picks: the phones don't send them.
setting.live.limits.1: Sorting shows the card and its tilt (11d), there's no separate draft. Instant blitz — answers only.
setting.live.points.0: Doesn't affect points: the verdict is preliminary, the game counts the final one at the reveal (with your judgement).
setting.live.tip.0: Don't read the verdict out loud before the reveal: only you see the console screen.
setting.live.tip.1: Fair play: players don't know you can see their picks before they submit. Reading them out or hinting based on them spoils the game.
setting.live.title: Live answers
setting.live.what: A panel on the console under the question: who has already answered and with what, and with the “👁 Live” switch — also what each player is picking, ordering or typing before “Send”. Only you see it: it's not on the stage or the phones.
setting.multiplier.limits.0: There's no multiplier in the final — it has stakes; there's none in “All in” and “Millionaire” either. In “Knockout” the multiplier works as in classic rounds.
setting.multiplier.points.0: Points for answers and penalties are multiplied, and on the board — together with the cell's ×2/×3.
setting.multiplier.tip.0: A last round with ×2 gives those who are behind a chance.
setting.multiplier.title: Points multiplier
setting.multiplier.what: All points of the round ×2 or ×3.
setting.newcomers.how.0: Before the game, “How to play” screens run on the stage, phones and console: phone, rounds, question types, buffs, debuffs, duels. You flip through them with “Next” or skip them with “To the game”.
setting.newcomers.how.1: Before each round the intro shows the “How the round works” reminder.
setting.newcomers.how.2: Before the first question of each type, the phone shows a tip on how to answer; the timer keeps running meanwhile.
setting.newcomers.tip.0: Turn it on for a new group; for regular players you can turn it off.
setting.newcomers.title: Explanations for newcomers
setting.newcomers.what: Short rules of this particular quiz for players who are playing for the first time.
setting.pacing.how.0: “Next” from the reveal, the table, round results and every “How to play” page — no sooner than after {paceStep} s; each next “100 to 1” row and bluff option — after {paceRow} s.
setting.pacing.how.1: “Start round” — {paceIntro} s after the round intro; “Close” a question early — {paceLock} s after it starts; “Skip turn” on the board and “Continue game” after a duel — after {paceStep} s.
setting.pacing.how.2: “Close the trial” in “Knockout” — {paceLock} s after it starts; “Start the ladder” in “Millionaire” — {paceIntro} s after the contestant is picked (by draw or by you); the “Decisions” screen in “All in” — {paceDecisions} s after the window closes.
setting.pacing.how.3: Until this time has passed, the button is inactive and fills up like a bar, and its hint says “Just a moment: players need to see the screen”. A double tap doesn't skip anything.
setting.pacing.how.4: “Pause” (the game is paused at once), “End round”, “End game”, removing a player, judging answers, adjusting points, debuffs, hints and dice all work immediately.
setting.pacing.tip.0: Press calmly: the button itself will show when you can move on.
setting.pacing.title: Minimum time before “Next”
setting.pacing.what: The game doesn't let you skip a screen: a host step that moves the game on only works after a short minimum time, so that everyone gets to see the reveal and the table.
setting.partial.how.0: Classic: at the reveal you can give a player “Partly”.
setting.partial.how.1: Board: “Partly” is available when judging out-loud answers and answers with manual checking, and ordering and numbers with a deviation get their share with automatic checking.
setting.partial.limits.0: There's no “partly” in a blitz, the final, “All in” and “Millionaire”; in “Knockout” it works as in classic rounds (but a partial answer counts as a mistake: the player goes “on the edge”).
setting.partial.points.0: The share is from 10 to 90% of the value (× the round multiplier).
setting.partial.points.1: Without this rule a nearly correct answer on the board gives 0. In classic rounds ordering and numbers with a deviation give a share automatically, even without the rule.
setting.partial.tip.0: Useful for “almost” answers: a surname without a first name, a year without a month.
setting.partial.title: “Partly” button
setting.partial.what: Gives you a “Partly” mark with a set share of the points.
setting.penalty.how.0: Players see the rule in the round reminder.
setting.penalty.limits.0: There's no penalty in the final — it has stakes; there's none in “All in” and “Millionaire” either. In “Knockout” the penalty works as in classic rounds.
setting.penalty.points.0: Classic: a minus only for a wrong answer given; silence — 0.
setting.penalty.points.1: Board: a minus for a mistake and for the silence of the player whose turn it is, on a normal cell.
setting.penalty.points.2: Blitz: a minus for each wrong try. Blitz cells don't have the round penalty — they have “Minus for all”.
setting.penalty.points.3: The penalty is multiplied by the round multiplier and the cell's mark. “Shield” turns the minus into 0.
setting.penalty.tip.0: With a penalty players hold back more often — good for “yes or no” questions.
setting.penalty.title: “Minus” penalty
setting.penalty.what: A wrong answer takes away the question's value.
setting.reveal.how.0: The picture emerges over the question's time on the stage and phones; a pause stops it, and “+15 s” doesn't slow it down: the reveal window is the question's initial time (including a longer audio clip).
setting.reveal.how.1: When answers are closed, the picture is complete. There's one answer.
setting.reveal.limits.0: Only “single choice”, “text” and “number”; only classic rounds and a normal board cell answered by phone.
setting.reveal.limits.1: Not together with video. Second try isn't available.
setting.reveal.limits.2: A crafty player with developer tools can see the original picture.
setting.reveal.points.0: An instant answer — 100% of the value, at the moment of full reveal — {revealMinShare}%, in between — evenly; later — also {revealMinShare}%.
setting.reveal.points.1: There's no speed bonus — it's already built in.
setting.reveal.points.2: A correct answer always stays correct for streaks, accuracy and achievements: the decline to 30% only reduces the points.
setting.reveal.points.3: The host's “correct” judgement doesn't give the full value either: the host decides whether the answer is correct, and the points decline by answer time, just as without the host.
setting.reveal.tip.0: Use recognisable pictures: logos, faces, places.
setting.reveal.tip.1: Blur is gentler, pixels are harder.
setting.reveal.title: Emerging picture
setting.reveal.what: The question's picture gradually becomes sharp: from pixels or from a blur.
setting.scores.how.0: The “Table” button on the phone shows the round columns “R1 R2 … Σ”. The name and total stay in place, the rounds scroll sideways.
setting.scores.how.1: Tapping your own row opens “+ / −”: answers (together with streaks and the speed bonus), mistakes (penalty), the final, duels, debuffs, your adjustments and undos (“Undone by the host”), and “All in”, “Knockout” and “Millionaire” bonuses. A player can't see anyone else's breakdown.
setting.scores.how.10: In a team game a row is a team; every team member sees their team's breakdown, and the “Your round” and “Your game” cards are the team's cards.
setting.scores.how.2: On the round results the stage writes “+N for the round” next to each row, and under the table — the best in the round and the biggest climb in the table.
setting.scores.how.3: On the console there's a collapsed “Points by round” panel: the round columns and anyone's “+ / −” with a tap.
setting.scores.how.4: In the game history — the same “player × round” table with “+ / −”, for old games too.
setting.scores.how.5: After each question the stage writes under the correct answer “4 of 7 correct · fastest — Olya, 2.1 s”, and in a bluff — whose fib got the most votes. The phone tells the player how fast their correct answer was, or how many answered correctly. There's no such line in the final, blitz and “Millionaire”.
setting.scores.how.6: On the round results — up to three “Round trivia” cards: ⚡ Lightning, 🎯 Sniper, 🔥 Streak, 🎭 Master of bluff, 🐑 Trusting soul, 🧠 Lone genius, 🧗 Hardest question — the first three that make sense. On the stage to the right of the table, on the phone and console — under it. The console also sees the share of correct answers for each question of the round.
setting.scores.how.7: The phone shows the player “Your round”: 4 of 6 correct, average time, fastest answer, the streak (if it isn't zero), from the second round on — the place before and after the round (“5 → 3”), and how many times they were fooled. A player can't see anyone else's card.
setting.scores.how.8: At the end the “Awards on stage” button shows “Game awards” after the podium — up to six categories, 4 s each; each tap shows the next. Without a host the awards run by themselves. Under their place the phone shows “Your game”: points by round, accuracy, best streak, fastest answer, and buffs, debuffs and bluff — if there were any.
setting.scores.how.9: In the game history — the same awards and a “player · accuracy · average time · best streak” table.
setting.scores.limits.0: Debuffs from the host don't count on the card — only bought ones. Time is only counted in questions with a timer.
setting.scores.points.0: Doesn't affect points: the breakdown only shows what the score is made of. The current question's points appear in it together with the table — after the reveal.
setting.scores.points.1: Trivia doesn't change points. A streak here means correct answers in a row, even without a streak bonus, and it's counted within a round: a new round starts it from zero.
setting.scores.tip.0: After the game, open the history: you can see in which round who pulled ahead.
setting.scores.title: Points by round, “+ / −” and trivia
setting.scores.what: The table shows how many points each player scored in each round, and the breakdown — where the pluses and minuses came from.
setting.spares.how.0: General spares (up to {maxSpares}) are used in classic rounds.
setting.spares.how.1: Each board category can have its own spares (up to {maxCategorySpares}). As soon as at least one category has them, each cell takes a spare only from its own category, and in a category without spares swapping isn't available.
setting.spares.how.2: While no category has its own, the board uses the general ones.
setting.spares.how.3: Spares are given out in turn, each only once per game.
setting.spares.limits.0: Simple types only (options, several correct, yes/no, text, number, slider), with no video, audio or emerging picture.
setting.spares.limits.1: These aren't the same as the survival questions of a “Knockout” round: those are set in the round itself and aren't used for swapping.
setting.spares.points.0: The value and time come from the question that was swapped: spares have no points or time of their own.
setting.spares.tip.0: There should be enough spares for everyone who takes a swap: at least as many as there are players.
setting.spares.title: Spare questions
setting.speedBonus.how.0: Players see the normal timer, the bonus is counted automatically.
setting.speedBonus.limits.0: Only classic rounds and “Knockout”, and only questions with a timer (not with video).
setting.speedBonus.limits.1: There's no bonus in a blitz, on the board, in the final, in “All in” and “Millionaire”; in “Knockout” it works as in classic rounds.
setting.speedBonus.limits.2: Not awarded on an emerging picture or on “Who am I?”.
setting.speedBonus.limits.3: Not awarded on a connection wall.
setting.speedBonus.points.0: An instant answer — 100% of the points, in the last second — 50%, in between — evenly.
setting.speedBonus.points.1: It also applies to partial points; on a spare question the time is counted from the moment of the swap.
setting.speedBonus.tip.0: Turn it off for questions that need thought — otherwise reaction speed decides.
setting.speedBonus.title: Speed points
setting.speedBonus.what: In a classic round a faster correct answer earns more points.
setting.streak.how.0: The player sees 🔥 with the length of the streak.
setting.streak.how.1: A streak is counted within a round; on the board — only for the player's own cells.
setting.streak.limits.0: There are no streaks in the final, “All in” and “Millionaire”; in “Knockout” they work as in classic rounds.
setting.streak.points.0: Starting from the set number of correct answers in a row, each correct answer adds a bonus: a percentage of its points or a fixed amount.
setting.streak.points.1: A partial or wrong answer or silence breaks the streak. In a blitz, not pressing doesn't break the streak.
setting.streak.points.2: With “Double points” the bonus is doubled too.
setting.streak.points.3: The “Safety net” buff stops a mistake breaking the streak.
setting.streak.tip.0: A streak of 3 answers and a bonus of 20–50% are noticeable but don't decide the game.
setting.streak.title: Streaks
setting.streak.what: A bonus for several correct answers in a row.
setting.undo.how.0: The “↶ Points” button in the console header opens the “Undo points” sheet: rounds and questions from newest, and in a question — rows like “Olya +200”, “Petro −100 (penalty)”, “Host: Ira +50”.
setting.undo.how.1: “Undo” next to a row cancels exactly those points. “Undo all” (points for the question) and “Undo round” ask first: “Undo the points of 6 players for round 2?”.
setting.undo.how.2: An undone row is crossed out, and next to it is “Restore”: the points come back, and the row can be undone again.
setting.undo.how.3: Players and the stage see a short notice “The host undid points: Olya −200 (question 7)” or “The host restored points: …”, and the table updates at once. An “Undone by the host” line appears in the “+ / −” breakdown, in the game history the undone points are crossed out and the undo is marked “↶”.
setting.undo.how.4: A question appears in the sheet as soon as you leave its reveal. At the reveal, change the judgement with the “Accept answer”, “Partly” or “Reject” buttons: that way the points are counted correctly.
setting.undo.how.5: In a team game a row is a team: the team's points are undone.
setting.undo.limits.0: In a game without a host there's no sheet: the author is a regular player and doesn't edit others' points.
setting.undo.limits.1: Polls and clouds give no points — there's nothing to undo there.
setting.undo.points.0: An undo is a separate “minus what was awarded” line, not a rewritten answer. The verdict stays (in the stats the answer is correct or not, as it was), and the streaks of later answers don't change. The final's stake limit follows the new score: a stake already placed that's higher than the new score is reduced to it.
setting.undo.points.1: The penalty for leaving the game can be undone too: it's the “(left the game)” row. After the game ends, only that can be undone.
setting.undo.points.2: An appeal decision too: the “(appeal)” row; undoing an answer also removes the appeal for that question. While the same player has a leaving penalty on this question, the appeal row can't be undone: undo the penalty first. After the game ends, appeal decisions can no longer be undone.
setting.undo.points.3: Answers in classic rounds, on the board, in a blitz and in the final (together with the penalty, streak and speed bonus) and your adjustments can be undone. Debuff purchases, duel stakes and “All in”, “Knockout” and “Millionaire” bonuses can't: they're format rules, not judgements. Nor can answers in “All in”, “Knockout” and “Millionaire” rounds.
setting.undo.tip.0: Made a mistake judging at the reveal? Just press a different mark. The sheet is for what's already past.
setting.undo.title: Undo points
setting.undo.what: A sheet on the console with everyone's points for each closed question and your adjustments. Wrong points are undone with one tap, and undone points can be restored.
team.answerer.how.0: In the editor, under “Team game”, choose “Who answers”: captain (as always), captain picks or in turn.
team.answerer.how.1: Captain picks: between questions the captain's phone has a strip “Answering: [Olya] [Petro] [Me]” and a “for the whole round” switch. Without the switch the choice is for one question, then it's the captain again; with the switch — until the end of the round.
team.answerer.how.2: In turn: the first question — the captain, then everyone in the team's order; whoever is offline is skipped. The captain can override the order with their own choice, then the queue stops, and the “Queue” button brings it back.
team.answerer.how.3: The choice applies from the next question. Nothing changes during a question, a vote or a trial.
team.answerer.how.4: If the chosen person is offline, the captain answers until they're back.
team.answerer.how.5: The phone of whoever answers says “You answer for the team”; teammates see “Olya is answering” and the draft live. The stage writes “Team — answering: Olya” (with more than three teams — briefly: “Team: Olya”), on the console there's a 🎤 next to that person in the team line-up; in “Live answers” — “acting: Olya”.
team.answerer.limits.0: Blitz (whoever pressed answers), duel (the duellist), polls and clouds (everyone individually) work as usual. There's no choice strip before them, and a “for the whole round” choice made earlier waits for the first question where someone needs to answer.
team.answerer.limits.1: Stakes, decisions (“All in”, “Millionaire”), buying and casting debuffs stay with the captain, even when someone else is answering.
team.answerer.limits.2: Between questions players only see their own next choice: for rivals the captain is shown there.
team.answerer.limits.3: In a game without a host it's all the same: the captain chooses from their phone, and without a choice the captain or the queue answers. The bot doesn't wait for anything.
team.answerer.points.0: Points go to the team as before: only who presses the buttons changes.
team.answerer.points.1: Whoever answers does: the answer (also in the final, “All in”, “Millionaire”, and on their team's cell), buffs, “Millionaire” lifelines and the chain hint, the second-try decision, moves in chains, sorting (with the card's tilt) and walls, the answer and doors in a “Knockout” trial, “Who am I?” clues and the drafts that teammates and the console see.
team.answerer.points.2: The captain keeps: picking the cell and the dice on the board, the final stake, “All in” and the decisions in “Millionaire”, debuffs (only the captain buys), duels and appeals, and choosing who answers.
team.answerer.tip.0: “In turn” lets everyone on the team play, and “captain picks” lets you give a question to whoever knows the subject.
team.answerer.tip.1: A debuff cast on a team works on the phone of whoever answers: that's where the answer field is.
team.answerer.title: Who answers
team.answerer.what: The captain can hand the answer to another person on the team: for one question or for the whole round. Or the game passes it round in a circle.
team.captain.how.0: The captain can be changed on the console at any time.
team.captain.how.1: The captain submits answers, stakes in the final, decides in “All in” and “Millionaire”, takes buffs, buys debuffs and declares duels. If “captain picks” or “in turn” is on in the quiz, the answer, buffs and moves pass to whoever answers.
team.captain.how.2: The rest of the team sees the captain's pick live on their phones, view-only; the stage and other teams don't see it.
team.captain.how.3: The host sees the captain's draft live in “Live answers” (with “👁 Live” on); the stage and other teams don't.
team.captain.how.4: In sorting, teammates see the captain's card and where they're dragging it; other teams don't.
team.captain.how.5: If the captain is offline, the captaincy passes to the next connected member; when they come back, they become captain again.
team.captain.limits.0: A debuff cast on a team works on the phone of whoever answers (without a choice — the captain's); the rest of the team sees a mark.
team.captain.points.0: Points go to the team, not the captain; accuracy and achievements come from the team's answers.
team.captain.tip.0: Make someone with a reliable connection captain; the rest give advice out loud.
team.captain.title: Captain
team.captain.what: The captain acts for the team: answers, stakes, decides. By default it's the first in the team's list.
team.dice.how.0: “Roll the dice” starts the round of rolls: everyone rolls on their phone, the stage shows the rolls.
team.dice.how.1: “Roll for the rest” rolls for those who are taking too long.
team.dice.how.2: Ties are re-rolled until all the results differ.
team.dice.how.3: The line-up is split into bands by descending rolls: the highest results go into the first team, the next into the second and so on, the lowest into the last.
team.dice.limits.0: While the rolls are going on, players can't be moved; changing the method cancels them. Rolling is possible when there are at least two in the lobby.
team.dice.points.0: The dice don't change points: all teams start from zero.
team.dice.tip.0: The most fun way to start an evening, when players don't know each other yet.
team.dice.title: Dice
team.dice.what: Everyone rolls a die on their phone, and players are divided into teams by the results.
team.formats.how.0: Classic, board, final, “All in”, “Knockout”, bluff, “100 to 1”, wall, sorting, chain, slider, pin, “Who am I?”: the captain answers (or whoever has been chosen — “Who answers”); tries and time are per team.
team.formats.how.1: Blitz: anyone can press, whoever pressed answers; the team shares its tries.
team.formats.how.2: Board: the captain picks the cell; on an out-loud cell anyone answers, and you mark the team's result.
team.formats.how.3: Final: one stake from the team's points, the captain stakes.
team.formats.how.4: “Millionaire”: the team becomes the contestant, the captain answers; the room is the other teams.
team.formats.how.5: Bluff: one fib and one pick per team.
team.formats.how.7: Buffs belong to the team; in “Ask the room”, members of other teams vote.
team.formats.how.8: A team buys debuffs with team points and casts them on another team — they work on whoever answers.
team.formats.how.9: Duels: team against team; the captain picks on their phone who from the team goes to the duel.
team.formats.points.0: The format's rules and points don't change: everything is counted per team, as for one player.
team.formats.points.1: Votes in polls and clouds come from people and give no points.
team.formats.tip.0: For big teams use more blitz and board: there the actions are shared out between people.
team.formats.title: Formats in teams
team.formats.what: All rounds and question types play in a team by their own rules; only who among the people acts changes.
team.host.how.0: Drag nicknames between the team columns on the console or choose a team in the list next to a nickname.
team.host.how.1: Players in the lobby see on their phone which team they're in, but can't change it.
team.host.how.2: Anyone left without a team goes into the smallest one at the start.
team.host.points.0: The split doesn't change points: all teams start from zero.
team.host.tip.0: Even out the strength: spread experienced players and newcomers across different teams.
team.host.title: I'll split them myself
team.host.what: You decide the team line-ups: you arrange the players on the console.
team.pick.how.0: In the lobby the phone shows team buttons with colours and names.
team.pick.how.1: A player can change their mind and pick another team before the game starts.
team.pick.how.2: You can move anyone on the console.
team.pick.limits.0: Anyone who hasn't chosen goes into the smallest team at the start.
team.pick.points.0: The choice doesn't change points: all teams start from zero.
team.pick.tip.0: Friends will end up together — good for a friendly game, but the teams' strength may turn out uneven.
team.pick.title: Players choose
team.pick.what: Everyone picks a team themselves with a button on their phone. This is the default way.
team.play.how.0: In the editor, turn on “Team game”, set the number of teams and their names.
team.play.how.1: In the lobby, choose how we form the line-up: I'll split them myself, players choose, random or dice. Anyone can be moved before the start.
team.play.how.2: Anyone left without a team at the start goes into the smallest team; empty teams don't play.
team.play.how.3: During the game the captain answers, or whoever has been chosen (see “Who answers”); the rest see the draft live on their phones and give advice out loud.
team.play.how.4: The stage and the table show the teams, with the line-up under the name.
team.play.limits.0: Teams — {minTeams}–{maxTeams}, a name — up to {teamName} characters.
team.play.limits.1: After the start the line-up doesn't change and new players can't join. A person can be removed; without its last person a team is out, along with its points.
team.play.points.0: Points go to the team. In their history and profile each member gets their team's place, points and win; accuracy comes from the team's answers. In the profile a member's podium follows the team's place.
team.play.points.1: Polls and clouds give no points, and everyone does them individually.
team.play.tip.0: For 6–12 players, 2–3 teams of 3–4 people work best.
team.play.tip.1: Dice is the most fun way to start an evening; “I'll split them myself” is for when you need to even out the strength.
team.play.title: Team game
team.play.what: Players join up in teams: a team answers as one player, and points, place and win are shared.
team.random.how.0: The line-up comes out even: team sizes differ by one at most.
team.random.how.2: Anyone who joined later is left without a team: press “Split into teams” again, or the game start will assign them.
team.random.points.0: The split doesn't change points: all teams start from zero.
team.random.tip.0: Press “Split into teams” when everyone is already in the lobby — then you won't have to reshuffle.
team.random.title: Random
team.random.what: The “Split into teams” button deals all players into teams at random.
